name: Runes of Summoning
summary: In the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Carendin Halgar gives warlocks runes for summoning a voidwalker. The ritual draws an unbound voidwalker into a circle, where an aspiring warlock can bend it to their will.

sections.title: Subjugation in the Magic Quarter
sections.body: Carendin Halgar gives the Runes of Summoning to warlocks ready to command a voidwalker. In the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, Forsaken practitioners study how to manipulate the Nether. A warlock casts the runes in the active summoning circle below Halgar's station. The ritual tears through the Void and draws forth a creature to be overpowered and bound into servitude.

faq.q: What are the Runes of Summoning used for?
aliases: what do runes of summoning do
how to use runes of summoning
faq.answer: A warlock uses the runes in the summoning circle in the Undercity's Magic Quarter to draw an unbound voidwalker from the Nether into the physical world. The warlock can then defeat it and bend it to their will.

faq.q: Who provides the Runes of Summoning?
faq.answer: Carendin Halgar, the Forsaken warlock trainer in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, provides the runes during the final stage of training to bind a voidwalker.

faq.q: Where must the runes be activated?
aliases: where do i use runes of summoning
faq.answer: Bring the runes to the purple summoning circle directly below Carendin Halgar's platform in the Magic Quarter.

faq.q: What happens after the entity is summoned?
faq.answer: The voidwalker attacks as soon as it is summoned. The warlock must subdue it with magic and arms. Once defeated, the entity is indentured, and Carendin Halgar teaches the permanent spell to summon it.

angles.text: As a warlock, you use the runes to prove your dominion over the Void, turning a chaotic shadow into an enduring, loyal minion.
As an Undead, you follow Forsaken practitioners into the Undercity's depths, where they bind void entities beneath the ruins of Lordaeron despite ancient taboos.
